newsitem.title: INDIA: Rising crop arrivals drag down India cotton prices.
newsitem.headline: Rising crop arrivals drag down India cotton prices.

text.p: Indian cotton prices fell on Monday on low demand and rising new crop arrivals, traders said.
They said daily arrivals in the Punjab region were up at 20,000-25,000 bales (170 kg each) and were expected to rise further after the Hindu Diwali festival.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid to 825/850 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) from 870/890 rupees. Punjab saw-ginned fell to 1,570/1,700 rupees from 1,590/1,750. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) eased to 18,600/19,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) from 19,000/19,500 rupees.
